name: My Webrequest
shortDescription: Create, test, and control browser request rules locally.
detailedDescription:
My Webrequest is a local-first request-rule manager for developers, QA engineers, support teams, and advanced users. Its focused full-page editor makes Manifest V3 rules understandable without requiring manual DNR JSON editing.

Create rules that block requests, redirect to fixed or capture-based destinations, upgrade HTTP to HTTPS, or remove and set request headers. Match with URL filters, wildcards, or regular expressions, then narrow behavior by resource type, request method, initiator domain, and priority. Built-in validation explains invalid patterns, conflicts, redirect cycles, permission state, and browser quota limits before a rule can misbehave.

Rules and settings remain on this device. There is no account, analytics, advertising, telemetry, remote code, cloud synchronization, or product-owned network service. Website access is optional and requested only for the concrete origins required when you enable a redirect or header rule. Safe blocking and HTTPS-upgrade rules do not require website access.

Export a checksum-protected JSON backup, preview a safe merge or full replacement before applying it, and recover the previous state after a replacement. The interface supports English, Simplified Chinese, Korean, Japanese, French, and Spanish, including keyboard navigation, reduced motion, increased contrast, and responsive layouts.
privacySummary: My Webrequest does not collect, transmit, sell, or share personal data. Rules, preferences, and recovery snapshots stay in browser extension storage on this device.
permissionSummary: Installation requests no website access. Storage keeps rules locally, declarativeNetRequest lets the browser enforce user-authored rules, and activeTab identifies the current site only after the user opens the popup. Optional host access is requested at enable time for only the concrete request and initiator origins a redirect or header rule requires.
chromeLegacyMigrationNote: Chrome users upgrading from the legacy My Webrequest release can review a deterministic migration report. Equivalent rules are imported disabled; unsupported or removed behavior remains explained and exportable and is never silently activated or discarded.
screenshotCaptions: Manage rules, runtime status, browser quotas, and precise match conditions in one focused workspace.
Review the exact website origins a rule needs before continuing to the browser permission prompt.
Verify backup integrity and preview safe merge or replacement effects before changing any rule.
